title: The Biggest Star In The Universe Makes Our Sun Disappear

scenes.voiceover: You think the Sun is big. But next to the largest star we have ever found, our Sun is a single, invisible pixel.
scenes.visualConcept: Host delivers the shock claim straight to camera.

scenes.voiceover: It is called Stephenson two eighteen. A red hypergiant so vast it barely fits inside your imagination.
scenes.visualConcept: A colossal roiling red hypergiant fills the frame.

scenes.voiceover: Drop it where our Sun is, and it would swallow Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and reach almost all the way to Saturn.
scenes.visualConcept: The giant star engulfing the inner solar system's orbits.

scenes.voiceover: You could fit about ten billion Suns inside it.
scenes.visualConcept: A tiny Sun dot beside the giant, count-up to 10 billion.

scenes.voiceover: It is so enormous that light itself, the fastest thing in existence, needs almost a full day just to travel around it once.
scenes.visualConcept: Host reacts to the light-speed fact.

scenes.voiceover: And stars this massive do not fade away quietly. They end as a supernova, one of the most violent explosions in the entire universe.
scenes.visualConcept: A star exploding into a brilliant supernova shockwave.

scenes.voiceover: Follow Mindwired for the universe that makes you feel small.
